content.title: Edit one results-header search parameter family on a dated Homes query
content.intent: Prove that a guest can change any one source-named parameter family already present in the Homes results header and refresh the results in place without returning to the homepage.
content.technique_notes: Techniques: state_flow because the promise is an in-place results-page edit followed by refreshed results without homepage navigation; eqp because destination, dates, and guests are the three source-named editable parameter families with the same expected outcome. Risk-judged interaction strength = 2 because no money, auth, or data-loss promise applies; covering array degraded to straight enumeration per tool note "strength=1 (degraded from 2: only 1 input(s))" for the single varying input edit_target. No budget ceiling supplied; this scenario was kept.

content.title: Add dates from the results header after arriving on Homes results without dates
content.intent: Prove that a guest who reached Homes results with destination and guests only can add valid dates later from the results header and stay on the results page.
content.technique_notes: Techniques: state_flow because the promise starts from an already routed results page and updates the active query in place; eqp because the source defines a supported omitted-dates class distinct from searches that already include dates. Risk-judged interaction strength = 2 because no money, auth, or data-loss promise applies. No budget ceiling supplied; this scenario was kept.

date_action: add valid check-in and check-out later

judgements.rationale: [value_score] Kept first because it exercises the core use-case promise across all three source-named editable parameter families and would hide defects if collapsed into only an add-dates flow.
[value_score] Kept second because the source explicitly names the no-dates start as a supported journey whose behavior differs from already-dated searches.
